html:
05 Prototype and software architecture

BMED Chapter 7.10 (programming, connectivity and simulations), 7.12 (prototype review and documentation), 6.5.1 (proof-of-concept prototypes) and Chapter 12 / IEC 62304 (software life cycle).

1. What was built

A single web application that runs all three concepts on one shared engine:

RouteConceptWhat the user does
#/OverviewCompare the three concepts; see the selected concept and why
#/concept-aA: Integrated monitorFull-screen patient-monitor display: stream a recording at 1–20× speed; alarm field, ECG / ART / PLETH channels, MAP forecast and trend channels, numeric boxes (HR, ART, forecast MAP, risk, R/C, treatment response), event list, soft-keys
#/concept-bB: Non-invasiveIdentical monitor layout and soft-keys; ART channel shows "not connected"; confidence-capped estimate and risk
#/concept-cC: Episode reviewSame monitor frame as a "review station": episode timeline, R/C, time in state, handoff summary, episodes, treatments; printable report and CSV/JSON soft-keys
#/evidence–Live verification results from evaluation/results/
#/design/...–This Design History File, rendered inside the app

Run it with scripts/run_app.sh and open <http://127.0.0.1:8765>. The server binds to localhost only by default.

2. Design choices and why

ChoiceReason (requirement or standard)
Python standard-library HTTP server; plain JavaScript with no framework and no CDNMinimises SOUP (IEC 62304 §8); works offline on a hospital network; nothing to patch
One engine for A, B and CFair comparison: differences come from the concept, not from implementation quality
Version 5 code vendored unchanged in src/; model SHA-256 compared with the verified value at start-up (mismatch = refuse to start, FMEA R-13)Traceability to the verified model; frozen SOUP item
Risk controls added in the app layer (app/engine/), not inside the modelEach control can be switched on or off and tested separately (doc 07, hazard H-09 layers)
Replay of recorded waveforms through a streaming windowSame code path as live streaming; repeatable tests; no live patient data needed
Only held-out recordings in the demo libraryA demo on training data would overstate performance
A and B share an identical layoutIEC 60601-1-8 / BMED 8.2.5.3: alarm position and controls must not move between modes
Concept screens are full-screen, non-scrolling patient-monitor displays (dark screen; alarm message field on top; waveform channels left; numeric parameter boxes right; soft-keys at the bottom)Match the clinician's existing mental model of a bedside monitor (BMED 8.2.5.3; Nielsen 2, match with the real world); a monitor never hides an alarm or value below the fold. Phones (< 900 px wide) get a stacked, scrollable version because a monitor layout cannot be read at that size
In-house Markdown renderer with escapingDocs cannot inject script; no extra dependency

3. Engine modules (app/engine/)

ModuleResponsibilityKey requirement
config.pyAll thresholds and constants in one place: MAP 70 / 65 / 55, persistence 2 up / 3 down, hysteresis 2 mmHg, 10 s window, 15 s horizonSPEC-02/03/04
recordings.pyLoad held-out simulated and VitalDB recordings; detect intervention onsets (sample-and-hold of sparse pump data, for event detection only)SPEC-09
model_service.pyWraps Version 5 HemodynamicPredictor; RC-07 raw pre-check; RC-09 shock-aware ABP check; domain-specific bias and sigmaSPEC-07, 11, 15
signal_checks.pyabp_artifact_free: rejects only true artefacts (steps > 80 mmHg, flat runs ≥ 0.2 s, pulse pressure < 5, impossible values)SPEC-15
alerting.pyIEC 60601-1-8 style alert state machine: levels, priorities, persistence, hysteresis, confidence cap, RC-08 fail-safe hold, RC-10 measured-pressure floor, technical SIGNAL CHECK, plain-language reasonSPEC-02–04, 07, 14, 15
intervention.pyEvent-log-driven response tracker: 30 s baseline, response window 30–60 s after onset, ΔMAP ≥ 5 mmHg or ΔR ≥ 10%, confounding flagsSPEC-09
session.pyReplaySession: one update per second → tick (forecast, alert, R, C, interventions, waveforms)SPEC-10
review.pyConcept C: whole-record review, episodes, narrative, server-side SVG report, CSV/JSONSPEC-13

Alert logic (Concept A)

LevelPriority (IEC 60601-1-8)Raised when (forecast MAP over the next 15 s)
STABLEnone≥ 70 mmHg
WATCHlow< 70, or falling ≥ 10 mmHg in 15 s
DETERIORATINGmedium< 65 (treatment target)
CRITICALhigh< 55
SIGNAL CHECKtechnical alarmno usable forecast and no usable measurement
  • Escalation needs 2 consecutive updates; de-escalation needs 3 updates and a 2 mmHg margin.
  • Confidence cap: a Low-confidence estimate can raise at most WATCH; Moderate, at most DETERIORATING.
  • RC-08 never lets a lower-confidence estimate lower an alert.
  • RC-10 never shows a level below what the measured arterial MAP itself indicates.

Uncertainty and risk score

  • σ is the calibrated forecast error (RMSE) for the active input regime and domain, fitted on validation data only.
  • P(MAP < 65) = Φ((65 − forecast) / σ).
  • Confidence: σ ≤ 12 mmHg → High; ≤ 20 → Moderate; otherwise Low.

4. Software of unknown provenance (SOUP, IEC 62304 §8)

ItemVersion (tested)Used forRisk if it failsMitigation
Version 5 model + code (src/)SHA-256 6fbec94f…Forecast, R, C, qualityWrong forecast (hazards H-09, R-01)Frozen; app-layer controls RC-07 to RC-10; full verification
PyTorch2.11.0Model inferenceWrong numbers / crashPinned; verification re-run on any upgrade; ONNX export available
NumPy2.5.3Signal arraysWrong numbersPinned
SciPy1.18.1Filters (Version 5 preprocessing)Distorted waveformPinned
pandas (3.0.6), tqdmas installedImported by Version 5 utilitiesImport failurePinned
Python3.14 (3.10+ supported)Runtime––
Evaluation only: scikit-learn, matplotlib, Playwright–AUROC, figures, UI testsNot shipped in the runtime–

The browser side uses no third-party code.

5. HTTP interface

Method and pathPurpose
GET /api/metaModel info, concepts, thresholds
GET /api/recordingsHeld-out demo library
POST /api/session {recording_id, concept, start_sec}Start a replay session (at most 24 at once, idle timeout 30 min)
POST /api/session/<id>/step {n ≤ 60}Advance n updates
POST /api/session/<id>/event {type}Clinician-marked intervention (Concept A)
DELETE /api/session/<id>End the session
GET /api/review/<id>[/report.html, /timeline.csv, /review.json]Concept C outputs
GET /api/verification, /api/selection, /api/docs[/name]Evidence and DHF

Hardening, all verified:

  • request bodies over 64 KB are rejected;
  • path traversal is blocked (tested with --path-as-is);
  • NaN is serialised as null;
  • unknown IDs return 404.

6. Demo library (held-out only)

IDStorySource

synthetic_4928Haemorrhage and resuscitationSimulated test split
synthetic_792Stable controlSimulated test split
synthetic_830Low complianceSimulated test split
vitaldb_5875, vitaldb_6131Surgery with vasopressor, hypotensionVitalDB test cases

vitaldb_5958Stable surgeryVitalDB test cases

They are chosen by scripts/build_demo_data.py using fixed rules, for example a normotensive start of 75–95 mmHg for deterioration stories.

7. Performance

MetricValueSpec
CPU latency per update, p50 / p95 / max11.9 / 175 / 318 msSPEC-10 ≤ 1000 ms marginal, ≤ 100 ideal → PASS (marginal)
GPU latency per update, p50 / p952.5 / 3.0 ms–
Concept C throughput5.7 s of compute per monitored hour (2 s step, GPU)–

8. Prototype review (BMED 7.12)

QuestionAnswer
What did the prototype prove?The model can drive a real-time, explained, fail-safe alert UI on CPU hardware; the three concepts can be compared on equal terms
What did it disprove?That Version 5's own quality gate is safe (R-01, H-09); that non-invasive forecasting is ready (Concept B)
What is "looks-like" vs "works-like"?Works-like for the software logic. Looks-like for monitor integration (replay instead of a live HL7 / IEEE 11073 feed)
What would a production version need?Live monitor interface; IEC 62304 class C process; cybersecurity (FDA 2023 guidance); summative usability study
